::: {.why}
The last two instrument families, and the two you will use as inputs rather than trade: the curve sets the discount rate behind everything in phase 4, and FX is where carry is easiest to see.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Given a bond's coupon, face value and maturity, write out its cash flow schedule and say what its price being below par tells you.
- State what a spot FX trade obliges each side to deliver, and where the interest rate differential shows up.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Watch the fixed income lecture from MIT 15.401 through discounting, yield to maturity and duration. Duration is the one concept here you will reuse, in phase 4, as a first-order sensitivity.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Plot the US Treasury curve from FRED on three dates you choose: one in 2019, one in mid-2020, and the most recent. Use DGS3MO, DGS2, DGS10 and DGS30. Say in one line which of the three is inverted and what that means as a statement about expected short rates.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the FX entry in the glossary: what EURUSD 1.08 means operationally, who delivers what in two business days, and the one sentence linking the forward points to the two countries' interest rates.
:::
:::
